NNS Governance API does not use protobuf anymore (in a previous [PR](https://github.com/dfinity/ic/pull/4843). Therefore, every `prost:*` can be removed from the API types file.

# What

* Replace `prost::Message` with `Debug, Default`
* Replace `prost::OneOf` with `Debug`

* Change from enum to i32 for some tests
  * This might seem "inconvenient" or "less readable", but note that it correctly reflects how the API is difficult to use right now, as the meanings of those i32's are not part of the API
* `DisburseMaturityResponse::amount_disbursed_e8s` was incorrectly not `pub` but using a method provided by prost. It is changed to `pub`
* Some `Option<T>` methods were accessed by methods using prost, which automatically `unwrap_or_default`. Added unwrapping.

author: tjprescott
body:
Fixes #10446.

This makes chunking automatic (no longer optional) based on the chunk size.

It aims to send consistently sized chunks to the LLM (configured for approximately 500 line) to ensure that the entirety of the API surface area gets adequately reviewed.

For chunks that exceed the size (for example, model namespaces), it will break that into sub-sections and append the "header" to each to retain the context.  For example:

```
# chunk 1
10: namespace models
11:   class Foo
12:   class Bar
   ...

# chunk 2
10: namespace models
511:   class Widget
512:  class Zoodle
```

Note this is likely to result in some potential comment duplication or some false positives (for example, the "you need sync and async clients" will likely crop up if they are contained in separate batches). However, we should be able to engineer away those discrepancies. 

The purpose of this change is to ensure that the LLM doesn't just "give up" making comments because the APIView is large... after all, that's what we do and why we want the AI to review it for us 😅

body:
The error #4620 was being raised when trying to index a match-all alert in the percolator index because a match-all alert doesn't have any filters or query string.

I suspect this alert was saved through the API, because on the frontend there is already a validation using the `alert_frequency` endpoint to prevent saving alerts that could potentially generate many hits.

On the frontend, this prevents saving match-all alerts:

![Screenshot 2025-04-25 at 3 50 31 p m](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/264bce2a-9ef3-4123-8b35-d725c9cf6bc9)

To solve this, I implemented a validation in both the frontend form and the Alert API serializer. This validation checks the query and raises an error if the alert is a match-all query. It works by removing the common parameters in alerts, specifically `type` and `order_by`. If, after removing these parameters, there are still other non-empty parameters, it means the query is not a match-all.


Frontend:
![Screenshot 2025-04-25 at 3 55 31 p m](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a6439d0-bf97-4f0c-99c6-45006e132734)


Alerts API.
```
{
    "query": [
        "You can't create a match-all alert. Please try narrowing your query."
    ]
}
```

A final question: Is it okay to not validate the alert frequency when saving a new alert via the Alerts API? I don't remember if there's a reason why we aren't doing this.

body:
This pull request adds the following functionalities to the harness test kit

### getHarnessAtIndex

This new function works acts like `getHarness`, but returns an instance of the harness corresponding to the matching element at the given index. This throws an error if the index is out of bounds.

Example usage:
```
// Retrieves the 4th option on screen
const option = await loader.getHarnessAtIndex(MatOptionHarness, 3);
```

### countHarnesses

This new function counts the number of matching component instances and returns the result.  

Example usage:
```
// Expect there to be five options on the screen
expect(await loader.countHarnesses(MatOptionHarness)).toBe(5);
```

### Filter by Label

New functionality makes it possible to fetch harnesses for certain form components using their floating label text. Previously, the user would have to either label the component with an id or class, or locate it in a form field using `MatFormFieldHarness.getControl()`.

This affects the following harnesses:
- MatInputHarness
- MatSelectHarness
- MatNativeSelectHarness
- MatDatepickerInputHarness
- MatDateRangeInputHarness

Example usage:
```
// template
<mat-form-field>
  <mat-label>Favorite food</mat-label>
  <input matInput value="Pizza"/>
</mat-form-field>

// test.ts
const input = await loader.getHarness(MatInputHarness.with({label: 'Favorite food'}));
```

body:
![Secured with Pensar](https://pensar-brand-assets.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/secured-by-pensar-large.svg)

The security issue was unsafe YAML deserialization, which could allow an attacker to inject a `!!js/function` and achieve Remote Code Execution.

**Fixes applied:**
- Changed the `JobSpec.action` type from a function to a string key representing a safe, predefined action.
- Introduced an `ALLOWED_ACTIONS` map: all allowed job actions must be declared in advance.
- In `/upload`, replaced `yaml.load(req.body)` with `yaml.load(req.body, { schema: yaml.FAILSAFE_SCHEMA })` to prevent support for dangerous YAML tags (`!!js/function`, etc.).
- Added validation that the YAML-parsed object is of the correct shape and that the `action` corresponds to an allowed key in `ALLOWED_ACTIONS`.
- The scheduled cron callback, as well as the `/run` endpoint, now call only the action from the `ALLOWED_ACTIONS` map, never deserialized code/functions supplied by the user.
- This completely closes the RCE vulnerability by strictly limiting the executable actions to only those defined in the application source.

That function is stored and then executed immediately via cron.schedule or the /run endpoint, resulting in remote code execution on the server. | critical | [Link](https://console.pensar.dev/testjosh/projects/pensar-goat-python/64adeb31-a9b7-4627-8bb4-edc051db48b0) |
